theme: A household with two kids and grandparents nearby
facts: Mia's birthday is on March 4th, and she likes a small party.
Leo's birthday is on November 19th, usually with a truck-shaped cake.
Hannah's birthday is July 9th, and she prefers a quiet dinner.
Ray's birthday is April 28th, and he loves grilled food.
Mia has a peanut allergy and carries an epinephrine pen.

Leo is allergic to milk and eggs, diagnosed at age two. At home his breakfast uses oat milk and only egg yolks. The school needs a copy of his allergy plan before the first day, and restaurants should be asked about dairy before ordering. His doctor expects many children to outgrow the allergy by six, but he must not test it himself.
Mia has piano lessons every Tuesday and Thursday at 4:30.
Leo has art class on Saturday mornings at the community center.

Mia goes to Maple Street Elementary across town. The school rule is that after-school activities need written permission, and any absence must be emailed to the teacher the day before. Late pickups must be arranged by text before 2 p.m. Permission slips for field trips are due one week early.
Leo's kindergarten opens at 8 a.m. and closes at 5:30 p.m.
Ray goes to the gym on Monday, Wednesday, and Friday at seven.

Hannah works as a nurse on rotating shifts, usually leaving at six in the morning and getting home by four in the afternoon on weekdays. Her shift schedule is posted on the fridge. She swaps shifts only with written notice to the charge nurse. When she works nights, Ray takes the morning school run.
Grandma Ruth lives two blocks away and visits for Sunday lunch.
The family car is parked in spot 23 in the building garage.

Dinner is usually at seven, with Hannah cooking and Ray doing the dishes. Leo's dishes are cleared by Mia after he finishes. On weekends, whoever stays home cooks, and takeout needs prior agreement. The house rule at the table is no phones, and everyone shares one good thing from the day.
Mia's teacher is Mr. Okafor, and his contact is in the class group chat.
Leo's blue backpack hangs on the hook by the front door.

Mia must be in bed by 9 p.m. on school nights and can stay up half an hour later on weekends. She reads for twenty minutes before lights out, and screens are only allowed after dinner and off by nine. If she has a piano lesson or a test the next day, bedtime does not change.
Leo naps from 12:30 to 2:30 every afternoon.

The big grocery run happens on the first weekend of each month, driven by Ray, with Hannah writing the shared list ahead of time. Frozen items go in last and into the freezer right away. Receipts go into the study drawer so the monthly budget can be checked at the end of the month.

When a child is sick, Ray stays home during the day and Hannah handles pickup after work. The shared insurance card lives in the study drawer. A fever above 38.5 Celsius requires a pediatrician visit, not waiting at home.
Ray makes weekend breakfast, and Hannah makes weekend lunch.
Online orders are delivered to the building's front desk.

Mia wants to join the science club next term, which needs a parent signature. Before signing, Hannah and Ray should check her timetable so the club does not clash with piano or homework. The club meets on Monday afternoons but asks for one outside field trip each month, which may take weekends.
